open_lines.statement: `parseOrders` returns one order per non-blank line, in line order
open_lines.open: Whether a whitespace-only line counts as blank, and how `\r\n` line endings are treated, are not stated; the requester settles it. Only lines that are empty (zero characters) are certainly blank.

open_lines.statement: A line is a list of `key=value` fields joined by `;`, and values are trimmed
open_lines.open: Whether whitespace around a key (e.g. `id=1; qty=2`) is accepted, and what happens with a repeated key, an unknown key, or a missing key, are not stated; the requester settles it. A line holding each of the five keys once, with no whitespace around keys, is the only form the request defines.

open_lines.statement: Each parsed order has `id`, `qty` and `price` as numbers
open_lines.open: What happens for an `id` that is not a number (e.g. `id=abc`) is not stated (no error class is named for it); the requester settles it.

open_lines.statement: `shippedAt` is the shipped_at text, `''` when empty
open_lines.open: A line with no `shipped_at` field at all (as opposed to an empty one) is not stated; the requester settles whether it equals an empty value.

open_lines.statement: A qty that is not a whole number of at least 1 throws RangeError naming the line
open_lines.open: Whether other spellings of a whole number (`2.0`, `1e2`, `+3`, `0x10`) are accepted is not stated; the requester settles it. Plain digit strings and the values above are the certain cases.

open_lines.statement: A price that is not whole cents of at least 0 throws RangeError naming the line
open_lines.open: Same as C-8 for other spellings of a whole number (`150.0`, `1e2`); the requester settles it.

open_lines.statement: A shipped_at that is not `YYYY-MM-DD` throws SyntaxError naming the line
open_lines.open: Whether a well-formed but impossible date (`2026-02-30`, `2026-13-01`) is rejected is not stated; the requester settles it. The shape four digits, `-`, two digits, `-`, two digits is the certain rule.

open_lines.statement: The line number in an error message is 1-based
open_lines.open: With blank lines in the text, whether "line" counts physical lines (the faulty order in `ok\n\nbad` is line 3) or non-blank lines (line 2) is not stated; the requester settles it. Where no blank line precedes the faulty one the two readings agree. Likewise, which error is thrown when one line has several faults is not stated; only lines with a single fault are certain.

open_lines.statement: `total` past the meter's limit lets the meter's LimitError through
open_lines.open: Whether `total` should avoid the error for lists over 10,000 orders is not stated and would conflict with one tick per order; the requester settles it. The meter's count is shared state: ticks from earlier calls in the same process also count toward the limit.

added_refusals.statement: The assignee must be a string or null
A name that is not a single line of text is refused

open_lines.statement: An agent is a non-empty name of at most 64 characters
open_lines.open: Whether a name made only of spaces counts as empty, and whether spaces around a name are trimmed before the length is counted or the name is stored (the existing requester and title fields are trimmed). The requester of the change decides; tests use names without surrounding spaces.

open_lines.statement: Resolved and closed tickets cannot be assigned or unassigned
open_lines.open: What a resolved or closed ticket answers when the request asks for the value it already has (the same agent, or `null` on an unassigned ticket): 409 or 200 with nothing changed. The requester decides; either way nothing changes, and tests check only the different-value case.

open_lines.statement: Each assignment change is one audit entry
open_lines.open: The entry's `action` name (such as `ticket.assigned`) is not fixed by the request or the audit decision; tests do not check it.

open_lines.statement: Assigning a ticket queues a notification for the assigned agent
open_lines.open: Whether the agent's name is a deliverable address or the relay maps it to one. The help desk's operators decide; the event's `to` is the agent's name.

open_lines.statement: `GET /tickets?assignee=<agent>` keeps that agent's tickets
open_lines.open: What a filter value over 64 characters, or with surrounding spaces, does (matches nothing, or 400 `invalid`, or is trimmed). The requester decides; tests use ordinary names.

open_lines.statement: The command-line table shows each ticket's assignee
open_lines.open: How an unassigned ticket's cell reads (empty, `-`, `unassigned`); the requester decides. Tests check only that it names no agent.

open_lines.statement: The first four columns of `list --raw` keep their positions
open_lines.open: Whether `list --raw` also shows the assignee, as a fifth tab-separated column after the title. The requester decides ("the command-line listing" may mean the table only); tests do not require a fifth column and do not forbid one.

open_lines.statement: With due times on, `GET /tickets?overdue=true` lists only open and in-progress tickets whose due time has passed
open_lines.open: The instant at which a ticket is exactly due (`due` equal to the current time). The loosest reading is that it is not yet overdue; the requester decides if "has passed" includes the exact instant. A check can be made at least one millisecond either side of `due`.

open_lines.statement: `overdue=true` combines with the other listing parameters
open_lines.open: The existing listing code combines `status` and `priority` with "either matches" rather than "both match", which is not what docs/api.md says. Whether to fix that is the requester's decision. This clause asks only that `overdue` is required in addition to whatever else is given, and that a ticket which is not overdue is never listed under `overdue=true`.

open_lines.statement: `overdue` values other than `true`
open_lines.open: Whether other values are refused as `invalid` (400), as a bad `status` is, or ignored, and whether `overdue=false` lists the tickets that are not overdue. The requester decides. A test must not assert either way.

open_lines.statement: The hours for each priority are configuration, not code
open_lines.open: The names of the settings and whether a restart is the way a change takes effect. The loosest reading is one environment variable per priority, read at start. The requester decides the names; a check must find them in the README configuration table, not assume them.

open_lines.statement: A value for the hours that the service cannot use stops it at start
open_lines.open: Whether zero, a fraction or a negative number is usable. Only a value that is not a number is required to be refused.

open_lines.statement: Existing tickets in the data file get due times from their own creation time and priority
open_lines.open: The hours used are those configured when the file is first started with the new release. Whether tickets that already had a due time and lost it (C-12) are given one by the same rule is the same question; this clause assumes yes.

open_lines.statement: The data file holds every ticket's due time before due times are switched on
open_lines.open: When the file is written. The loosest reading is that the file holds them after the service has started and stopped normally; a deploy that must be checked before switching on relies on this. The requester decides if an operator has to run a separate step instead.

open_lines.statement: After a rollback and a new upgrade, tickets are not left without due times
open_lines.open: 1.4.0 drops fields it does not know when it saves, so tickets that existed before the rollback may lose `due` in the file it writes. What to do with these is decided by the requester. The only requirement here is that no ticket is left without a due time and that a ticket whose `due` survived keeps it.

open_lines.statement: The data file stays one that 1.4.0 starts on and shows every ticket from
open_lines.open: What the key for the due time is called in the file. Any key that 1.4.0 loads without refusing is acceptable.

open_lines.statement: With `DUE_TIMES` not `on`, the API answers exactly as 1.4.0 does
open_lines.open: Whether `on` is case-sensitive (`ON`, `On`). The loosest reading is that exactly `on` switches due times on and the request's wording is `on`; the requester decides about other spellings. A check should use `on` and unset only.

open_lines.statement: Creating a ticket does not change its audit entry or notification because of due times
open_lines.open: Whether `due` should be recorded in the audit log is for the requester to decide; it is not required.

open_lines.statement: The command line and the weekly report keep working on a data file that holds due times
open_lines.open: Whether `show` or `list` should print the due time, and whether that depends on `DUE_TIMES`. The request does not ask for it, so it is not required; the requester decides.

added_refusals.statement: A due time cannot be set by a client

open_lines.statement: An operator can change the hours for each priority in the service's settings, without a code change; an unset or empty setting means the hours in C-1
open_lines.open: the names of the four variables, whether a change must take effect without a restart, and who may change them are not in the request; the requester decides. The names are documented (C-27).

open_lines.statement: A hours setting the service cannot use stops it at start with a message naming the variable
open_lines.open: whether `0` and fractional hours (`1.5`) are usable; whether the same refusal applies while `DUE_TIMES` is not `on` (the request says the service then answers "exactly as it does today", which started with any value). The requester decides.

open_lines.statement: An hours setting too large for a due time to be represented stops the service at start, like C-4, instead of failing later
open_lines.open: the exact largest accepted value; the requester decides, any cap below the runtime limit is acceptable.

open_lines.statement: `GET /tickets?overdue=true` lists only tickets that are `open` or `in_progress` and whose due time has passed
open_lines.open: what `overdue` means with a value other than `true` (`false`, `1`, empty): ignored, or 400 `invalid` in the envelope, or the opposite listing. The request defines only `true`; the requester decides. No check relies on any other value.

open_lines.statement: `status` and `priority` filtering without `overdue` behaves as it does today
open_lines.open: docs/api.md says combined filters must all match, but `matchesFilters` in src/tickets/query.js lists a ticket matching either. Whether to fix that is the requester's; nothing here depends on it.

open_lines.statement: Due times are switched on only by `DUE_TIMES=on`
open_lines.open: what other values do (`ON`, `1`, `true`, `off`): treated as not on, or refused at start. The requester decides.

open_lines.statement: The data file holds every ticket's due time once the new release has started on it, with `DUE_TIMES` not yet `on`
open_lines.open: whether operators prefer an explicit one-off migration instead of a write at start; the requester decides. Whatever is chosen, the observable result for an operator, using only the new release, is a file that holds every due time while `DUE_TIMES` is not `on`.

open_lines.statement: The operator command line and the weekly report keep working on a file that holds due times
open_lines.open: whether `list` or `show` should also print the due time. Nothing is required by the request beyond the API; the requester decides.

added_refusals.statement: A due time never makes a request fail

open_lines.statement: The response hours are configurable, per priority, without a code change
open_lines.open: The names of the four settings are not given. The builder chooses them and documents them in the README table; a test must find them there, not assume them. What range of hours is accepted (zero, fractions, an upper limit) is the requester's to decide; a test uses whole numbers of hours from 1 to 1000 only.

open_lines.statement: A ticket created while DUE_TIMES is off still gets its due time in the data file
open_lines.open: The field's name in the data file is not given; `due`, the same as the API, is the builder's choice and a test may check it only through the restart.

open_lines.statement: Until DUE_TIMES is `on`, the service answers exactly as 1.4.0 does
open_lines.open: What the service does with a DUE_TIMES value that is neither `on`, `off`, unset nor empty (for example `ON`, `yes`, `1`): treat as off, or refuse to start under the rule of C-6. The requester decides; a test uses only `on`, `off`, unset and empty.

open_lines.statement: `GET /tickets?overdue=true` lists only the open and in-progress tickets whose due time has passed
open_lines.open: Whether a ticket is overdue at exactly the instant of its `due` is not given ("has passed" suggests later than `due`); a test does not check that instant.

open_lines.statement: The overdue listing is paged and combines with the other filters like any listing
open_lines.open: Today's code combines `status` and `priority` with "or", not "and" as docs/api.md says (`matchesFilters` in src/tickets/query.js). Whether to correct that is the requester's to decide; this clause is about `overdue` only, and a test of `overdue` combined with another filter uses a combination that gives the same answer under both readings, or the stated "every" rule.

open_lines.statement: A value of `overdue` other than `true` is not specified
open_lines.open: Whether `overdue=false` lists the tickets not overdue, all tickets, or is `invalid` (400, as an unusable `status` is today) is the requester's to decide.

added_refusals.statement: A field with a key that is not `id`, `qty`, `price`, `status` or `shipped_at` throws SyntaxError naming the line
A key that appears twice in one line throws SyntaxError naming the line
`id` must be a whole number of at least 0, else RangeError naming the line
`id`, `qty` and `price` must not exceed 9007199254740991 (`Number.MAX_SAFE_INTEGER`), else RangeError naming the line
A `shipped_at` in the right form must also be a real calendar date, else SyntaxError naming the line
A non-array argument to `total` throws TypeError and ticks the meter zero times
A resolved or closed ticket refuses even an assignment that would change nothing
`assignee` must be present in the body
`assignee` must be a string or `null`
A refused request changes nothing and tells no one
The service answers an `overdue` value other than `true` with 400 `invalid` when due times are on
The service does not start when it cannot save the due times it has to add to the data file
The new release does not write anything into the data file that 1.4.0 checks and refuses
With `DUE_TIMES=on`, `overdue` must be `true`
If the data file cannot be written at start, the service does not start
A start that cannot save the stamped file does not serve
